title: Markup Dictionary
subject: ui
summary: Generated from docs/consumer/developer/markup-dictionary.md by scripts/markup-dictionary-elements.ts; the markdown stays until that script is ported.

purpose.intro: The contract between components/pages and the theme engine. Every valid attribute, every valid value, and what you must not do.

reference.statement: A DOM node carries **either** `element` or `layout`, never both. Axis attributes (`emphasis`, `status`, `state`, `scale`, `concept`) can be added to either. `position` can be added to either as well: it is the markup axis, not a theme one (see below).

claims.text: Real dimensions (a sidebar's width, a field's width, an avatar's size, a container's measure), paddings and gaps are the theme's: a value, per element, per breakpoint. Markup never carries a number, with one exception: `Stack`'s `gap` and `pad`, the spacing of a composition, which take a number or a CSS length (layouts.md § Stack). Compositions (a header over two columns over a footer) use `Stack`; a single surface uses `position`. `className` and inline `style` are deprecated and are not a place for spacing or sizes.
**Sunset.** `className` on a library component is deprecated in favour of `position`. It is still accepted; nothing enforces this yet. The migration of the pages comes later.

reference.statement: `position` says where a surface stands in its parent and how much of it it takes. Markup positions; the theme sizes. Every value is one fixed set of structural classes (`web/components/src/lib/position.ts`); the theme never reads the attribute. Several values are space-separated.

reference.statement: Format: `element="{family}--{element}"`. Generated from `shared/libs/ui/types/elements.ts` by `shared/libs/ui/scripts/markup-dictionary-elements.ts`; do not edit by hand. Each row lists the axes the element carries: `all` is the full set from `types/axes.ts`, `–` means the axis does not apply, anything else is the subset. `concept` is always allowed. Typography identities (`type--…`) are a separate vocabulary.

reference.statement: Transient states (`hover`, `active`, `focus`) are CSS pseudo-classes only — never set as attributes.
Default when absent: `md`. Affects padding, typography, icon size. Never colors.
Values are product-defined: `"knowledge"`, `"dashboard"`, `"settings"`, etc. Set on a wrapper element — descendants inherit the visual overrides.

claims.text: Use axis attributes for visual variation
Use Tailwind structural utilities for positioning (`flex`, `grid`, `gap-*`, `w-*`, `h-*`, `items-*`, `justify-*`, `overflow-*`)

reference.topic: Rules › What components MUST NOT do

claims.text: No inline styles for visual properties
No hardcoded colors, fonts, shadows, radii
**Simple components** (Button, Checkbox): native element is the root, receives all theme attributes directly.
**Compound components** (input + toggle, input + icons): wrapper div is the root surface. Native elements are children styled via inheritance.
